key_insight: GFlowQEC learns to propose promising quantum LDPC codes, increasing the yield of new top-scoring codes per expensive evaluation.
engineering_relevance: A pretrained code proposer could stretch limited quantum-code evaluation budgets by concentrating searches on promising candidates.
method: Build lifted-product codes one group element at a time with a generative flow network.
Train on earlier search scores to sample codes in proportion to a power of their score, then freeze the model.
Rank batches of proposed codes before paying to evaluate selected candidates.
evidence_signal: For distance-scored, 180-physical-qubit codes, ranking 10 draws per paid evaluation found over 2× as many new top-scoring codes as tuned parallel tempering and over 3.5× as many as a supervised screen ranking 10 random candidates.
watch_item: The advantage is setup-dependent: a supervised screen won at 100 candidates, soft Q-learning matched or exceeded GFlowQEC, and distance-based results do not establish circuit-level performance.
paper_title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
